title: Unramifiedness tested at rational points of geometric fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and a geometric point $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-geometric-point], put $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, with projections $p_s:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $g_s:X_s\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $f$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism] if and only if, for every such $\Omega,s$ and every morphism $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X_s$ with $p_s\circ x=\mathrm{id}$, the morphism $p_s$ is unramified at the image of $x$, meaning on some open neighbourhood of that point. Every $z\in X$ admits such $\Omega,s,x$ with $g_s(x)=z$ and $\Omega$ an algebraic closure of $\kappa(z)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The quantifier on $\Omega$ allows extensions transcendental over $\kappa(f(z))$. No flatness, local finite presentation, quasi-compactness, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed; an empty source satisfies the criterion.

source.place: Tag 0475 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-unramified), together with schemes.tex Tag 01J9 (lemma-characterize-points) for field-valued points.

proof.text: For $z\in X$, choose an algebraic closure $\iota:\kappa(z)\to\Omega$ by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], the pair $(z,\iota)$ gives $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with image $z$. Put $s=f\circ a$, a geometric point by [def-weil-geometric-point]. The pair $(a,\mathrm{id})$ satisfies $f\circ a=s\circ\mathrm{id}$, so [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $x=(a,\mathrm{id}):\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X_s$ with $g_s\circ x=a$ and $p_s\circ x=\mathrm{id}$. Its image $y$ therefore has $g_s(y)=z$. This proves the lifting clause without any algebraicity assumption over $\kappa(f(z))$.

source.place: Tag 01J9 (lemma-characterize-points), preceding description by pairs; fibre-product universal property, Tag 01JP (definition-fibre-product)

proof.text: Write $W_f$ for the union of unramified source neighbourhoods in [lem-trf-unramified-locus-base-change]. For each geometric $s$, independently of whether $f$ is unramified, [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change] makes $p_s$ locally of finite type, and the locus lemma gives $W_{p_s}=g_s^{-1}(W_f)$. If $f$ is unramified, $X$ itself occurs in that union, hence $W_f=X$ and $W_{p_s}=X_s$. In particular every test section has image in an unramified source neighbourhood for $p_s$.

Conversely assume the test condition. For any $z\in X$, take $s,x,y$ from Step 1. The hypothesis gives $y\in W_{p_s}$, because it supplies an open unramified neighbourhood of $y$. Apply the equality $W_{p_s}=g_s^{-1}(W_f)$ of [lem-trf-unramified-locus-base-change], with the locally finite type hypothesis for $p_s$ already checked in Step 2. This gives $z=g_s(y)\in W_f$. Since $z$ was arbitrary, $W_f=X$.

Thus $X$ is covered by opens on which $f$ is unramified. On each such open take the affine unramified charts in the equivalent affine-cover formulation of [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Their union is an affine unramified covering for $f$ itself; the ring maps are unchanged on these charts. That same formulation proves $f$ unramified. If $X$ is empty this is the empty affine cover; the test and lifting clauses are vacuous, so the argument includes that case.

lean.statement: theorem unramified_iff_geometricPoint_test {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] : (IsUnramified f ↔ ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ pullback f s), x ≫ pullback.snd f s = 𝟙 (Spec (.of Ω)) → ∃ U : (pullback f s).Opens, x (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω) ∈ U ∧ IsUnramified (U.ι ≫ pullback.snd f s)) ∧ (∀ z : X, ∃ (s : Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure (X.residueField z))) ⟶ S) (x : Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure (X.residueField z))) ⟶ pullback f s), x ≫ pullback.snd f s = 𝟙 (Spec (.of (AlgebraicClosure (X.residueField z)))) ∧ pullback.fst f s (x (IsLocalRing.closedPoint (AlgebraicClosure (X.residueField z)))) = z)
